es.summary: Alteración del tejido muscular que produce debilidad, dolor y, en casos graves, parálisis.
key_points: Puede ser hereditaria, inflamatoria o inducida por fármacos (p. ej., estatinas).
Elevación de creatina quinasa (CK) es el hallazgo de laboratorio más frecuente.
El manejo incluye retirar la causa, fisioterapia y control del dolor.
Complicaciones graves incluyen insuficiencia respiratoria y caídas.

pathophysiology: Daño a la membrana sarcolemal por inflamación, toxicidad o mutaciones genéticas.
Liberación de enzimas musculares (CK, aldolasa) al torrente sanguíneo.
Degeneración de fibras musculares y sustitución por tejido fibroso o graso.
risk_factors: Uso de estatinas lipofílicas (p. ej., atorvastatina).
signs_symptoms: Debilidad muscular progresiva, especialmente en proximales.
Calambres y fatiga al realizar actividades cotidianas.
En casos severos, dificultad para respirar.
diagnostics: CK sérica ↑ (puede superar 5‑10 veces el límite normal).
EMG muestra descargas de fibrilación y ondas positivas.
Biopsia muscular para confirmar inflamación o cambios estructurales.
Pruebas genéticas cuando se sospecha miopatía hereditaria.
treatment: Suspender o cambiar fármacos causantes (p. ej., estatinas).
Corticosteroides o inmunosupresores en miopatías inflamatorias.
Fisioterapia y ejercicios de fortalecimiento progresivo.
Analgesia con paracetamol o AINE según tolerancia.
complications: Insuficiencia respiratoria por debilidad del diafragma.
Caídas y fracturas por pérdida de fuerza y equilibrio.
Dependencia funcional y disminución de la calidad de vida.
nursing_care: Evaluar fuerza muscular (escala de Oxford) y nivel de actividad.
Monitorear CK y signos de dolor o inflamación.
Implementar medidas de prevención de caídas y posicionamiento adecuado.
Administrar analgésicos según prescripción y observar efectos adversos.
Coordinar fisioterapia y registrar progreso en ADL.
patient_teaching: Informar sobre la relación entre estatinas y dolor muscular; reportar síntomas tempranos.
Enseñar ejercicios de estiramiento y fortalecimiento seguros.
Explicar la importancia de evitar sobrecarga y descansar cuando haya fatiga.
Indicar cuándo buscar atención (dolor intenso, dificultad respiratoria, aumento de CK).

evidenced_by: dificultad para realizar actividades de la vida diaria
outcomes: Movilidad: nivel de independencia – paciente realizará ADL con asistencia mínima en 7 días.
Seguridad: prevención de caídas – paciente no presentará caídas durante la hospitalización.

interventions.action: Evaluar fuerza muscular usando la escala de Oxford cada 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar la debilidad y medir la respuesta al tratamiento.

interventions.action: Promover ejercicios de estiramiento y fortalecimiento bajo supervisión de fisioterapia.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la fuerza y previene contracturas.

interventions.action: Colocar al paciente en posición semisentado y cambiar de posición cada 2 h.
interventions.rationale: Reduce el riesgo de contracturas y mejora la ventilación.

interventions.action: Implementar medidas de prevención de caídas (pasamanos, calzado antideslizante).
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la probabilidad de lesiones por caídas.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de reportar dolor o debilidad nuevos.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección temprana de empeoramiento.

outcomes: Seguridad: prevención de caídas – paciente permanecerá sin incidentes de caída durante su estancia.
Movilidad: nivel de independencia – paciente mantendrá la capacidad de caminar con ayuda mínima.

interventions.action: Evaluar el riesgo de caídas usando la escala de Morse al ingreso.
interventions.rationale: Identifica factores de riesgo y guía intervenciones específicas.

interventions.action: Mantener el entorno libre de obstáculos y bien iluminado.
interventions.rationale: Reduce oportunidades de tropiezos.

interventions.action: Colocar la cama en posición baja y usar barandillas laterales.
interventions.rationale: Previene caídas al intentar levantarse.

interventions.action: Proveer dispositivos de asistencia (bastón, andador) según necesidad.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la estabilidad al deambular.

interventions.action: Reforzar la educación sobre levantarse lentamente y usar apoyo al cambiar de posición.
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la hipotensión ortostática y el riesgo de desmayo.

en.summary: Alteration of muscle tissue that produces weakness, pain, and in severe cases paralysis.
key_points: It can be hereditary, inflammatory, or drug-induced (e.g., statins).
Elevated creatine kinase (CK) is the most common laboratory finding.
Management includes removing the cause, physiotherapy, and pain control.
Severe complications include respiratory failure and falls.

pathophysiology: Damage to the sarcolemma membrane from inflammation, toxicity, or genetic mutations.
Release of muscle enzymes (CK, aldolase) into the bloodstream.
Degeneration of muscle fibers and replacement with fibrous or fatty tissue.
signs_symptoms: Cramps and fatigue during daily activities.
diagnostics: Serum CK ↑ (may exceed 5‑10× the upper limit).
EMG shows fibrillation potentials and positive sharp waves.
Muscle biopsy to confirm inflammation or structural changes.
Genetic testing when hereditary myopathy is suspected.
treatment: Discontinue or switch causative drugs (e.g., statins).
Corticosteroids or immunosuppressants for inflammatory myopathies.
Analgesia with acetaminophen or NSAIDs as tolerated.
complications: Falls and fractures from loss of strength and balance.
Functional dependence and reduced quality of life.
nursing_care: Assess muscle strength (Oxford scale) and activity level.
Monitor CK and signs of pain or inflammation.
Implement fall prevention and proper positioning measures.
Administer analgesics per prescription and monitor adverse effects.
Coordinate physiotherapy and document progress in ADL.
patient_teaching: Inform about the link between statins and muscle pain; report early symptoms.
Teach safe stretching and strengthening exercises.
Explain the importance of avoiding overload and resting when fatigued.
Indicate when to seek care (severe pain, breathing difficulty, CK rise).

evidenced_by: difficulty performing activities of daily living
outcomes: Mobility: independence level – patient will perform ADL with minimal assistance within 7 days.
Safety: fall prevention – patient will not experience falls during hospitalization.

interventions.action: Assess muscle strength using the Oxford scale every 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Allows quantification of weakness and measurement of treatment response.

interventions.action: Promote supervised stretching and strengthening exercises with physiotherapy.
interventions.rationale: Improves strength and prevents contractures.

interventions.action: Position the patient semi‑upright and change position every 2 h.
interventions.rationale: Reduces contracture risk and improves ventilation.

interventions.action: Implement fall prevention measures (handrails, non‑slip footwear).
interventions.rationale: Decreases likelihood of injury from falls.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of reporting new pain or weakness.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection of worsening.

outcomes: Safety: fall prevention – patient will remain fall‑free during stay.
Mobility: independence level – patient will maintain the ability to walk with minimal assistance.

interventions.action: Assess fall risk using the Morse scale upon admission.
interventions.rationale: Identifies risk factors and guides specific interventions.

interventions.action: Keep the environment free of obstacles and well lit.
interventions.rationale: Reduces tripping opportunities.

interventions.action: Set the bed to a low position and use side rails.
interventions.rationale: Prevents falls when getting up.

interventions.action: Provide assistive devices (cane, walker) as needed.
interventions.rationale: Improves stability while ambulating.

interventions.action: Reinforce education on slow rising and using support when changing positions.
interventions.rationale: Reduces orthostatic hypotension and fainting risk.

summary.0.quote: Muscle disorders can cause weakness, pain or even paralysis.

key_points.0.quote: Causes of muscle disorders include: Injury or overuse, such as sprains or strains , cramps or tendinitis A genetic disorder, such as muscular dystrophy Some cancers Inflammation, such as myositis Diseases of nerves that affect muscles Infections Certain medicines Sometimes the cause of muscle disorders is unknown.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Atorvastatin is a lipophilic (fat-soluble) statin, which may allow it to penetrate the muscle tissue and lead more readily to myopathy.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: A group of muscular disorders called muscular dystrophy are caused by genetic mutations.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Primary symptom is muscle weakness, first affecting the proximal muscles and later affecting muscles of the extremities.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Myalgia, or muscle pain, is common and occurred in 5%–10% of clients taking statin therapy in observational studies (Grundy et al., 2019).

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Eventually, ALS causes complete loss of control over voluntary movements including walking, talking, eating, and even breathing.

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: Some examples of disorders that might be diagnosed using muscle biopsy include inflammatory myopathies (e.g., polymyositis, dermatomyositis) and specific types of muscular dystrophy.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Genetic Testing Many neuromuscular disorders have a genetic component, meaning they can be inherited from parents.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Corticosteroids or immunosuppressants can also be used to help limit production of antibodies.

sections.complications.0.quote: Results in eventual respiratory failure due to scoliosis and diaphragmatic muscle weakness.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Report any muscular signs and symptoms to their health care provider, including muscle pain, muscle weakness, and very dark urine, which can indicate rhabdomyolysis.
